<security_assessment>

<details>
This is a minimal patch to the file(1)/libmagic project's configure script. It changes the line `LDFLAGS=""` to `LDFLAGS="${LDFLAGS}"` on one platform-specific branch of the configure logic. This is a standard, benign packaging fix: instead of wiping out LDFLAGS that the distribution or packager has set (e.g., hardening flags like `-Wl,-z,relro,-z,now`), the build system now preserves and carries them forward.

There is no malicious behavior here. The change performs no command substitution, no `eval`, no obfuscation, no network access, and no file system manipulation outside of normal build configuration. The `"` entities are simply escaped double-quote characters in the patch text, an artifact of the XML transport format, not hidden code. The `LDFLAGS="${LDFLAGS}"` construct is plain variable preservation, not dangerous environment evaluation.

Overall, this patch is an example of good packaging hygiene (preserving user-supplied build flags) and contains no evidence of tampering or supply-chain attack.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
